messages:
maria: heads up - our blob-rotation job wrote a small subset of prod backups to the archive bucket without SSE-KMS headers. detected via spot-check of new archive objects.

satish: omg. how many objects?

maria: ~120 objects across 3 tenants, all from yesterday's rotation window. sizes look normal. metadata shows missing `x-amz-server-side-encryption` and `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`.

eva: @maria can you paste an example metadata line?

maria: here you go:

```
> Key: backups/tenant-42/2026-03-20/backup-2026-03-20T03-12-07.tar.gz
> Content-Length: 2.4GB
> x-amz-meta-origin: db-cluster-primary
> x-amz-server-side-encryption: 
> x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id: 
```

sam: suspicious - the rotator uses the k8s serviceaccount `blob-rotator-sa` which should call kms:Encrypt on write. any recent RBAC/KMS grant changes?

satish: I rolled an RBAC cleanup last week and removed an older `backup-agent` grant. but `blob-rotator-sa` should still have a grant. I'll check policy history.

infra-bot: deploy:blob-rotation v2.3.1 rolled 2026-03-19 02:45 UTC (sha: c4d2f6) by ci/cd

maria: timeline looks like v2.3.1 + RBAC cleanup overlapped. either the new binary changed S3 put behavior or the principal lost kms:Encrypt grant.

eva: check cloudtrail/audit for PutObject calls during the rotation window. specifically inspect kms:Encrypt events and kms:Grant usage.

maria: pulled CloudTrail snippet - PutObject shows 120 successful puts, but kms:Encrypt shows 0 corresponding operations.

sam: that implies the client didn't request encryption rather than KMS rejecting it. who changed the rotator config? there was a config flag `preserve-sse` we toggled in the last merge request.

satish: i can confirm - MR #1127 set `preserve-sse=false` to avoid double-encrypting when copying between object stores. I assumed metadata forwarding would be handled elsewhere.

maria: so the rotator explicitly strips SSE headers when copying. combined with a separate process that expected copies to be encrypted by a later step -> gap.

eva: this is a policy + code bug, not a KMS compromise. still high severity because unencrypted backups exist. next steps: 1) pause rotator, 2) isolate the affected objects, 3) restore encrypted copies from previous snapshots if available, 4) run a re-encrypt job that reads object, decrypts (if applicable), and writes with SSE-KMS header, 5) rotate CMK for affected tenants?

sam: added checklist to incident channel runbook. a few clarifications: if original source copy was unencrypted at rest on the source, we can't recover encrypted bytes - must re-encrypt from plaintext copy. do we have plaintext?

maria: source db snapshots for those tenants are intact in the snapshot-store (they were created before rotation). we can re-run copy+encrypt from snapshot-store.

satish: I'm going to re-grant a short-lived kms:Encrypt permission to `blob-rotator-sa` and run a scoped re-encrypt for the 120 objects. will use an ephemeral grant with TTL 1h.

eva: also add audit changes: CloudTrail currently drops debug copy logs due to sampling. we need to ensure PutObject/KMS usage are logged at INFO and that our SIEM alerts on any PutObject without SSE header for backup prefixes.

maria: assigned: satish -> re-encrypt job, sam -> rollback rotator config to `preserve-sse=true` and add unit tests, eva -> audit alert and CloudTrail retention check, oncall -> runbook escalation for customer comms if needed.

oncall: got it. i'll prep a short customer note template in case any tenant requires disclosure. tentatively low-impact internally but still a P1 for encops.

satish: quick note on mitigation: I'll run this with KMS GenerateDataKey then PutObject with `x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms` to ensure S3-managed server-side encryption with CMK. Will capture PutObject requestIDs and attach to audit ticket.

maria: also: add a new pre-deploy canary that copies a small test object and verifies SSE headers are preserved. we need integration test for cross-region copy path.

eva: security follow-up: update least-privilege guidance in RBAC cleanup playbook to warn about metadata-forwarding effects.

sam: any vuln triage notes? not exploitability but a process vulnerability. mark as CVE-N/A, internal postmortem and go-live gated by tests and audit rules.

maria: agree. will open postmortem and link to this thread. tagging @infra-bot to create a ticket: `ENCOPS-rotate-unencrypted-backups-700123`

infra-bot: created ticket ENCOPS-700123: "blob-rotator metadata-preserve bug -> unencrypted backups" assigned to satish, sam, eva. due: 2026-03-22

sam: thanks. i'll hold the rotator rollout until we have the re-encrypt run and the CloudTrail alert in place. :thumbsup:
